extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials and staff who manage or plan interactions with the private sector and advisory committees (committee managers, agency heads, legal/ethics staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) applies to meetings, groups, and interactions between Executive branch officials and private-sector participants, and the required procedures when FACA applies. Covers illustrative scenarios, establishment, membership, meetings, and documentary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: information or viewpoints vs collective advice/recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA does not apply where the purpose is to obtain information or viewpoints from individual attendees as opposed to advice, opinions or recommendations from the group acting in a collective mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative Scenario One: meetings to obtain experiential and anecdotal information from individual corporate executives (no solicitation of collective advice or recommendations) are not covered by FACA. Anti-pattern: soliciting or treating group responses as collective advice will push the interaction toward FACA coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective deliberation/advice triggers FACA
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA applies when a committee is established to meet, interact, deliberate, and advise an agency official or other federal officers — i.e., when the group is used to provide advice or recommendations in a collective mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative Scenario Two: establishing a committee of senior corporate officials that will deliberate and advise on NPR issues is covered. A committee structure with core membership and subgroups that interact/deliberate is an example of collective advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment by an agency head to obtain advice
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee established by an agency head to obtain advice or recommendations for him/her or other federal officers falls within FACA coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key test: whether the committee was created (or used) by an agency official to obtain advice/recommendations. If so, additional FACA requirements apply (charter, notice, DFO, minutes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership composition: not composed wholly of federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA applies when the committee is not composed wholly of full-time, or permanent part-time federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a group consists entirely of federal full-time/permanent part-time employees, FACA generally does not apply; inclusion of non-federal-members (e.g., private-sector executives) makes FACA coverage more likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership balance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When FACA applies, the membership must be balanced in terms of points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance requirement means composition should reflect a range of perspectives relevant to the committee's mission. This informs appointments and chartering; imbalance can raise legal or management issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member ethics obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may be subject to applicable ethics laws depending on their appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance notes that appointments can trigger ethical restrictions or disclosure obligations; agencies should review ethics applicability when appointing non-federal members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter approval required before meetings or action
rubrics_metrics.description: No advisory committee can meet or take action prior to the Administrator approving a charter, and appropriate notifications and filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishment process: obtain charter approval and complete required filings before convening a committee. Failure to charter before meeting is a procedural violation of FACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/agency authority to establish committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator is authorized to establish advisory committees to advise him/her on functions vested in the Administrator by the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act or other GSA authorizing legislation; committees also may be established by specific statutory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee creation must rest on proper statutory or delegated authority; where statute explicitly establishes a committee, that statutory basis governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice: 15 days advance Federal Register announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings must have 15 days advance notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should publish Federal Register notices at least 15 days before meetings. This is a statutory/administrative precondition for public meetings under FACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open meetings requirement (public access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings must be open to the public unless limited statutory bases for closure apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule is openness; closures are allowed only on narrowly defined statutory grounds. Agencies must justify and document any closure under applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Federal Officer attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: A Designated Federal Officer (DFO) must be in attendance at advisory committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFO presence is required to ensure agency control/oversight and procedural compliance. Agencies must designate and ensure the DFO attends meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committees must have minutes which are available for public inspection (except for portions of a meeting which were closed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes should document proceedings and be retained/posted for public inspection in accordance with FACA; closed sessions may redact or withhold portions consistent with allowable closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in function or static membership increases FACA risk
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA coverage could become an issue if the function/mission of the group changes over time and the Administrator begins to use the group as a source of collective advice or recommendations; the more static the group composition (same attendees at each meeting), the more likely FACA applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor recurring groups: a series of meetings initially framed as information-gathering can evolve into a de facto advisory committee if the role, use, or membership becomes consistent and collective advice is relied upon.
